title: RAW personified arts bind distinct prerequisite omissions to futile pursuit
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_EXECUTED. Salzburg M III 36 gives two written futility claims: an unspecified learner ignorant of partes tends toward arts in vain, while teachers without Logic cultivated her sister arts in vain. Preserve the speaker, absent competence, studying actor and activity; do not infer that possessing the prerequisite guarantees success.

design.mechanism: Bind a figure-owned first-person or local art frame to a negative prerequisite, retain the actor attempting the downstream activity, and preserve the written futility consequence. Grammar's Qui nescit partes / frustra tendit ad artes and Logic's Frustra doctores sine me coluere sorores are two source instances with different prerequisite expressions and actor descriptions. The same generic necessity idea is already retained elsewhere; this proposal retains this particular illustrated repeated argument with its speaker/learner/teacher distinctions.
design.unit: Complete owned published Salzburg Universitaetsbibliothek M III 36 unit236r–243v, all16 whole institutional images viewed; focal complete art faces239v and240v, each reread whole once after first-note freeze. Retain all seven art pages239v–242v, theology wagon243r, planet/age/hour series236r–239r and cosmos/Albertus ending243v. No assumption that catalogued blank244r/v are published or inspected.
design.contrast: R1: a static list of art names with no dependency. R2: mere temporal precedence rather than a negative prerequisite. R3: swap the ignorant/omitting actor and the art, or let me change speaker independently of the local labeled figure. R4: turn necessary competence into a sufficient guarantee of successful study. R5: infer a single literal timber object continuously transformed across every picture, beyond the written evidence.
design.prediction: A source-content account must preserve that the learner who does not know partes is also the actor tending toward arts in vain, and that the doctors are the actors cultivating sister arts while Logic is absent. Reassigning me to Priscianus, Aristotle or another art changes which resource is omitted; reversing necessary and sufficient would assert an outcome the source does not give. The two clauses should remain recognizably comparable without making their different actors and omitted prerequisites identical. Mere repetition of art labels cannot supply these consequences.
design.scope: Exploratory source-only content hypothesis. No Voynich values, role map, count projection, target test, new primitive requirement or independent attestation. Informed same-witness reading with prior project/status/old-card exposure. Historical rhetorical claims about study, not experimentally verified educational laws.

source_basis.native_reading: 239v clear native Latin: Qui nescit partes / frustra tendit ad artes. 240v clear native Latin: Frustra doctores sine me coluere sorores. Spelling/abbreviation expansions are provisional; partes as grammatical components and sorores as sister arts are context-supported interpretations, not separately labeled equation definitions.

assumptions_and_costs: Native labels bind the adjacent speaking art frame; no full diplomatic transcription or textual edition has been established.
Grammar's large German verse is crossed out and has a smaller red replacement above. The RAW relies on the uncancelled Latin clause, not on silently restoring the canceled verse.
Logic's upper German text discusses discerning whether speech is true or false; exact intervening wording and its lower second Latin clause remain partly uncertain. No missing syllogism is invented.
Grammar's unknown partes and Logic's omitted me are related negative-prerequisite constructions, not two identical controlled input/output observations.
Direct source pictures show woodwork, wheels and joint wagon roles. Continuity of one physical material object across the individual art pages is an inference and is not required by this proposal.
No success consequent is supplied for a learner possessing Grammar or Logic. No causal mechanism of learning, scholastic curriculum schedule or medical application is inferred.
Catalogue date/location are contextual attribution, not identity with Laufenberg, the Voynich manuscript or a uniquely independent tradition.
